terms.definition: The 23.5° lean of Earth's axis away from vertical, relative to its orbital plane; the entire cause of seasons.
The point in Earth's orbit where a hemisphere's lean toward or away from the Sun is at its maximum, giving the longest or shortest day of the year.
The point in Earth's orbit where neither hemisphere leans toward the Sun, giving close to equal day and night everywhere.
The latitude directly under the Sun at solar noon; it swings between +23.5° and -23.5° across the year as Earth orbits.
How many hours of sunlight a given latitude receives on a given day, which grows or shrinks with the season.
